Built and shipped a production RAG + NL2SQL system that turns plain-English questions into governed SQL and grounded answers over live business data.
:::

## The problem

Stakeholders needed answers from data they couldn't query themselves, and hand-written reports couldn't keep up. The system had to translate natural-language questions into correct SQL and ground its answers in retrieved context — reliably enough to trust in front of the business. [[TODO: one sentence on who used it and the decision it supported.]]

## The finding

```{python}
#| label: fig-hero
#| fig-cap: "Answer accuracy across question types, before vs. after retrieval grounding + NL2SQL guardrails. Replace with your real eval."
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

cats = ["lookup", "aggregation", "multi-table", "temporal"]
before = np.array([0.71, 0.52, 0.38, 0.44])
after  = np.array([0.94, 0.86, 0.72, 0.79])
x = np.arange(len(cats)); w = 0.38
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.2))
ax.bar(x - w/2, before, w, color="#c0c4cc", label="baseline LLM")
ax.bar(x + w/2, after,  w, color="#2563eb", label="RAG + NL2SQL guardrails")
ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(cats)
ax.set_ylabel("answer accuracy"); ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
ax.legend(frameon=False)
for s in ["top", "right"]: ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color("#d5d5df"); ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#d5d5df")
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#eef0f4", lw=1)
plt.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("hero.png", dpi=120, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor="white")
plt.show()
```

The hard questions (multi-table, temporal) are where naive prompting fails — grounding and SQL guardrails are what made those trustworthy. [[TODO: replace the numbers above with your real eval-set results.]]

## Decisions and tradeoffs

I split the problem into retrieval (grounding answers in the right context) and NL2SQL (generating governed queries), rather than asking one prompt to do everything — that made each half testable and each failure debuggable. [[TODO: your stack — vector store, embedding model, LangChain vs. custom, and why.]] Guardrails on the generated SQL (schema-constrained, read-only) traded a little flexibility for a lot of safety.

## How it works

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the retrieve → generate SQL → answer flow (sketch)"
#| eval: false
# Replace with a readable slice of your real pipeline.
def answer(question: str) -> str:
    ctx = retrieve(question)            # vector search over docs/schema
    sql = nl2sql(question, schema)      # schema-constrained, read-only
    rows = run_readonly(sql)
    return synthesize(question, ctx, rows)
```
